explanation.text: The Logic: Vega is the option Greek that measures the sensitivity of an option's price to changes in the implied volatility of the underlying. Formally, Vega = ∂C/∂σ — the change in option price for a one-percentage-point change in implied volatility. Higher implied volatility generally raises option prices (both calls and puts), and Vega quantifies how much that price moves for a given change in volatility. The Trap: Interest sensitivity is captured by Rho, not Vega. Time decay is measured by Theta. The change in Delta per unit change in the underlying is Gamma. Only "volatility sensitivity of option price" matches Vega's definition. Note: The cited page of the NISM-Series-XXI-B Portfolio Managers workbook (p.294) mentions delta, gamma and vega as options-based portfolio sensitivity measures but does not explicitly define vega as the sensitivity of option price to implied volatility in the pages checked. The framing above is general options-Greeks knowledge.
